The area of each of the four congruent L-shaped regions of this 100-inch by 100-inch square is 3/16 of the total area. How many inches long is the side of the center square?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a large square, with a centered small square inside; from the four sides of the small square, line segments respectively extend to the boundary of the outer large square, dividing the region outside the center square into four mutually congruent L-shaped regions. The problem states that the outer large square is 100 inches × 100 inches, and that the area of each L-shaped region is 3/16 of the total area. Reasoning: The total area of the outer large square is 100^2 = 10000 square inches. The area of each L-shaped region is (3/16) × 10000 = 1875 square inches. The total area of the four L-shaped regions is 4 × 1875 = 7500 square inches. The center square in the figure is exactly the remaining region, so the area of the center square is 10000 - 7500 = 2500 square inches. Therefore the side length of the center square is sqrt(2500) = 50 inches.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: a 100-by-100 outer square is partitioned into a central square and four congruent surrounding L-shaped regions, one near each corner/side. Read from the text that each L-shaped region has area 3/16 of the total area. Compute the total outer area as 100^2 = 10000 square inches. One L has area (3/16)(10000)=1875, so the four L-shaped regions together have area 4*1875=7500. Since the image shows the central square is exactly the remaining region inside the outer square, its area is 10000-7500=2500. The side length of the central square is sqrt(2500)=50 inches.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the diagram shows a large square with a smaller square centered inside it, and the remaining border-like space is split into four congruent L-shaped pieces. Work only with fractions of the total area. From the text, each L-shaped piece is 3/16 of the whole square, so the four L-shaped pieces together occupy 4*(3/16)=12/16=3/4 of the whole. Therefore the center square occupies the remaining 1/4 of the whole square's area. Because the center region is a square and the outer region is also a square, the ratio of their side lengths is the square root of the ratio of their areas: sqrt(1/4)=1/2. The outer square side is 100 inches, so the center square side is (1/2)*100=50 inches.
